title: Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff
what_it_is: Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff

sections.label: Commission on Parliamentary Service schemes
sections.summary: A Commission was set up to consider revisions to Parliamentary Service schemes of service arising from Civil Service pay revisions announced on 20 February 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: A Commission was set up to consider revisions to the schemes of service of the Parliamentary Service arising from the Civil Service pay revisions announced on 20 February 2026.

sections.label: Report recommends Parliament staff salaries
sections.summary: The Report recommends Parliament staff salaries adopt the same adjustments as civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008), plus a retention payment for Parliamentary Clerks.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Report recommends that the salaries of the Parliament staff adopt the same salary adjustments as civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008) and a retention payment component for Parliamentary Clerks.

sections.label: Parliamentary and Language Executive Schemes
sections.summary: The Commission recommends the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) adopt the same salary adjustments, also with effect from 1 August 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Commission recommends that the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) adopt the same salary adjustments, also with effect from 1 August 2026.

sections.label: PSD salary adjustments announcement
sections.summary: The Report highlights that PSD announced salary adjustments of 2% to 9% depending on market gaps to help the Public Service attract and retain talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the Report highlights, the PSD announced salary adjustments of 2% to 9% depending on market gaps to help the Public Service continue to attract and retain talent to deliver well for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Proposed retention payment parameters
sections.summary: The proposed retention payment has clear parameters, a fixed quantum of roughly 1.5 to 1.75 months' salary per year, annual and three-year payouts, a 20-year cap, and a one-off ex-gratia payment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed retention payment is a practical and thoughtful response.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is designed with clear parameters, a fixed quantum, roughly equivalent to 1.5 to 1.75 months' salary per year, annual payouts for entry level Clerks and three-year payouts for those recognised for competence, but capped at 20 years, and a one-off ex-gratia payment to support the transition.

sections.label: Parliament determines terms of service
sections.summary: Under article 5(51)(6) of the Constitution, Parliament must determine the terms of service after receiving the Commission's advice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under article 5(51)(6) of the Constitution, Parliament must determine the terms of service after receiving the Commission's advice.

sections.label: Report proposes pay and retention
sections.summary: The Report proposes adopting PSD's Management Executive Scheme adjustments with higher discretionary bonuses and a retention payment component.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Here, what is proposed in the Report comprises essentially of two parts: first, adopting the same adjustments adopted by PSD for the Management Executive Scheme, as well as higher discretionary bonuses to recognise and encourage strong performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, introducing a retention payment component to attract and retain talent, as set out in paragraph 10 of the Report.

sections.label: Remote voting and support passed
sections.summary: Members voted by standing and placards, and with Parliament staff's help passed nearly $100 billion in support for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For instance, we were not in our actual seats, so we had to vote by standing up and saying "yes" or "no" or "abstain" on placards, and Parliament staff would record every vote to reflect the democratic will of our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This task they did with fortitude, and with their help, we passed nearly $100 billion in support for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Need to attract Parliamentary talent
sections.summary: The speaker argues for attracting and retaining talent, citing recognition, remuneration and responsibility, and urges unanimous support for the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: All these combined shows how the need for a cutting-edge Parliament has become all the more obvious in the last 10 to 15 years, and if demands on our elected Parliamentary Members has increased, and rightfully so, because demands have increased, then what more the need to attract and retain good talent to support this process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To recap, this is about recognition, remuneration and responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of these three arguments, I urge all Members to support this worthy Motion unanimously.
